questions.q: What three tests must a side hustle idea pass?
a: It must be feasible, profitable and persuasive
It must be cheap, fast and popular
It must be novel, risky and scalable
It must be fun, social and legal
questions.why: Lesson 1 names feasibility, profitability and persuasiveness.

questions.q: What does feasible mean in the summary's test?
a: You can run it in an hour a day and see results soon
It needs no money at all to start
It can replace your full-time job
It has no competitors in the market
questions.why: Lesson 1 asks whether you can do it in an hour a day and get results within a week.

questions.q: Which three parts make up an offer?
a: A promise, a pitch and a price
A logo, a slogan and a website
A product, a discount and a guarantee
A target, a budget and a deadline
questions.why: Lesson 2 builds the offer from price, pitch and promise.

questions.q: What should the promise do, according to the summary?
a: State a bold benefit people can see right away
Explain every feature in fine detail
List your qualifications and experience
Describe the history of the company
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the promise should be bold and immediately beneficial.

questions.q: Which four items belong on the launch shopping list?
a: Website, one social profile, scheduling tool and payment system
Website, ad budget, office space and a lawyer
Logo, business cards, accountant and bank loan
Email list, blog, podcast and online course
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists the website, one profile, a scheduler and a payment tool.
